title: AI & Machine Learning Privacy Hardening Checklist
metaDescription: Complete checklist to protect your privacy when using AI tools like ChatGPT. Secure your data from AI training and surveillance.
intro: AI tools like ChatGPT collect vast amounts of personal data for training and improvement. This checklist helps you minimize data exposure, opt out of AI training, and maintain privacy while using artificial intelligence services.

items.task: Disable ChatGPT conversation history
items.why: Prevents OpenAI from storing your conversations and using them for model training.
items.howTo: Go to ChatGPT Settings > Data Controls > Chat History & Training and toggle off 'Chat History & Training'. This stops saving new conversations.

items.task: Delete existing ChatGPT conversations
items.why: Removes previously stored conversations that may contain sensitive information.
items.howTo: In ChatGPT sidebar, click the three dots next to each conversation and select 'Delete'. Or use Settings > Data Controls > Export/Delete to bulk delete.

items.task: Opt out of AI model training across platforms
items.why: Prevents your data from being used to train future AI models without your consent.
items.howTo: For ChatGPT: Settings > Data Controls > Improve the model for everyone (toggle off). For other AI tools, check privacy settings for similar training opt-out options.

items.task: Review data policies of AI tools you use
items.why: Understanding what data is collected helps you make informed decisions about AI tool usage.
items.howTo: Read privacy policies for ChatGPT, Claude, Bard, and other AI tools. Look for data retention periods, training usage, and sharing practices.

items.task: Use privacy-focused browsers for AI interactions
items.why: Reduces tracking and fingerprinting when accessing AI services online.
items.howTo: Use a privacy-focused browser or similar privacy-focused browsers when accessing AI tools. Enable strict tracking protection and disable third-party cookies.

items.task: Never input sensitive personal information
items.why: AI systems may store, analyze, or inadvertently expose personal data in responses to other users.
items.howTo: Avoid sharing names, addresses, phone numbers, financial info, medical details, or confidential work information in AI chats.

items.task: Opt out of facial recognition databases
items.why: Facial recognition AI systems use your photos for training and identification without explicit consent.
items.howTo: Submit opt-out requests to Clearview AI, PimEyes, and other facial recognition companies. Use services like DeleteMe for bulk opt-outs.

items.task: Restrict photo sharing on social media
items.why: Social media photos are commonly used to train AI models and facial recognition systems.
items.howTo: Set social media profiles to private, limit photo tagging, and avoid posting clear face photos. Review existing photos and delete unnecessary ones.

items.task: Learn to identify AI-generated content
items.why: Protects you from deepfakes, AI-generated misinformation, and manipulated media.
items.howTo: Use tools like AI or Not, FakeSpotter, or Sensity to detect AI-generated images and videos. Look for common AI artifacts like unnatural skin texture or inconsistent lighting.

items.task: Remove personal data from AI training datasets
items.why: Data brokers sell personal information that ends up in AI training datasets.
items.howTo: Submit removal requests to major data brokers like Acxiom, LexisNexis, and Spokeo. Use automated services like Incogni or Privacy Bee for comprehensive removal.

items.task: Secure voice assistants and AI devices
items.why: Voice assistants continuously collect audio data that can be used for AI training and surveillance.
items.howTo: Disable always-listening features, regularly delete voice recordings, and review voice assistant privacy settings. Mute devices when not in use.

items.task: Disable location-based AI features
items.why: Location data helps AI systems build detailed profiles of your behavior and preferences.
items.howTo: Turn off location services for AI apps, disable location history in Google/Apple accounts, and use airplane mode when not needed.

items.task: Review company AI usage policies
items.why: Understanding workplace AI rules helps prevent accidental data breaches and policy violations.
items.howTo: Request AI usage guidelines from IT/HR. Understand what AI tools are approved, prohibited, and how company data should be handled.

items.task: Keep personal and work AI usage separate
items.why: Prevents cross-contamination of personal and professional data in AI systems.
items.howTo: Use different accounts/browsers for personal vs. work AI tools. Never use personal AI accounts for work tasks or vice versa.

items.task: Never input confidential work information
items.why: AI systems may store and potentially expose sensitive business information to competitors or unauthorized parties.
items.howTo: Avoid inputting client names, proprietary processes, financial data, or confidential projects into AI tools. Use generic examples instead.

items.task: Maintain records of AI tool usage
items.why: Creates accountability and helps identify potential data exposure incidents.
items.howTo: Keep a log of which AI tools you use for work, what types of information you input, and business purposes. Review regularly with supervisors.

items.task: Understand AI-powered employee monitoring
items.why: Many companies use AI to monitor employee productivity, behavior, and communications.
items.howTo: Ask HR about AI monitoring tools in use. Review employee handbook for AI surveillance policies. Understand your rights and any opt-out options.

items.task: Use privacy-focused AI tools for work
items.why: Some AI tools offer better privacy protection and data handling for professional use.
items.howTo: Consider enterprise versions of AI tools with stronger privacy controls, or alternatives like Claude for Slack, Bing Chat Enterprise, or locally-hosted AI solutions.

items.task: Use VPN when accessing AI services
items.why: VPNs mask your IP address and location, making it harder for AI companies to build location-based profiles.
items.howTo: Connect to a reputable VPN service before using AI tools. Choose servers in privacy-friendly countries and avoid free VPN services that may log data.

items.task: Create separate accounts for different AI use cases
items.why: Prevents AI systems from building comprehensive profiles by limiting data correlation across different activities.
items.howTo: Use different email addresses and accounts for work AI, personal AI, creative projects, and research. Use temporary email services when possible.

items.task: Conduct monthly AI privacy audits
items.why: AI privacy policies and features change frequently, requiring regular review to maintain protection.
items.howTo: Monthly: review AI tool privacy settings, check for new opt-out options, delete unnecessary conversation history, and update privacy preferences.

items.task: Request your AI data periodically
items.why: Understanding what data AI companies have about you helps identify privacy gaps and enforcement needs.
items.howTo: Submit data access requests to major AI companies quarterly. Review what data they have, how it's used, and request deletion of unnecessary information.

items.task: Explore local AI solutions
items.why: Running AI models locally keeps your data private and eliminates cloud-based privacy risks.
items.howTo: Try local AI tools like GPT4All, LM Studio, or Ollama for basic AI tasks. These run entirely on your device without sending data to external servers.

pro_tips: Set calendar reminders to review AI privacy settings monthly - companies frequently update policies and add new data collection features.
Create a 'burner' email specifically for AI tool signups to isolate AI-related communications from your main email accounts.
Before sharing AI-generated content, verify it doesn't contain hidden personal information that might have been used in the generation process.
Use a privacy-focused browser with strict privacy settings when accessing AI tools to minimize tracking and fingerprinting across sessions.
Keep a privacy journal documenting which AI tools you use and what information you share - this helps identify patterns and potential risks over time.
